# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

# Reference palette

This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
is system-agnostic — **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.

## How to use these values

Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
reference them by role throughout — so the light/dark values swap in one place,
and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:

```css
.viz-root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
  --text-secondary: #52514e;
  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
  /* …only the roles this chart uses */
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
    --text-primary:   #ffffff;
    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
    --series-1:       #3987e5;
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
  --text-primary:   #ffffff;
  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
  --series-1:       #3987e5;
}
```

Declare the dark values under both scopes as above — the media query covers
the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
which must win both ways (the `:not(…)` guard lets a light stamp beat
OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).

## Categorical palette

Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
dark surface, not a separate palette:

| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
|------|-----|-------|------|
| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |

This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
(OKLab ×100, ≥8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 19.6 light / 19.3
dark (≥15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors — with all 28 pairs in
play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule — so those
chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
in both modes** (worst pair CVD ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
light / 20.9 dark — clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
dark band (OKLCH L ≈ 0.48–0.67, ≥ 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening —
the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
dark run in the 6–8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
this order deliberately trades that fourth slot — yellow now sits beside orange —
for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow↔orange
confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
pure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full
gate.

The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic — candidate
orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
choose only among the passing ones.

## Sequential hue

Default single hue: **blue**, light→dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
one-hue ramp.

| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |

The full 100→700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude —
heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks —
funnel stages, tiers — validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).

## Diverging pair

(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue↔aqua was

"""Shared metric engine for the Bluebell SaaS investor update.

Single source of truth: every derived number in the deck, the Excel model and
the board-deck reconciliation comes from here.
"""
import openpyxl

SRC = "data/financials.xlsx"
STARTING_CUSTOMERS = 120


def load(path=SRC):
    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)["raw"]
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True))
    out, prev = [], STARTING_CUSTOMERS
    for m, mrr, new, churned, cogs, sm, hc in rows:
        beg = prev
        end = beg + new - churned
        prev = end
        out.append(
            dict(month=m, mrr=mrr, new=new, churned=churned, cogs=cogs, sm=sm,
                 headcount=hc, cust_beg=beg, cust_end=end)
        )
    return out


def enrich(d):
    """Add per-month derived metrics in place and return the list."""
    for i, r in enumerate(d):
        r["arr"] = r["mrr"] * 12
        r["gross_profit"] = r["mrr"] - r["cogs"]
        r["gm"] = r["gross_profit"] / r["mrr"]
        r["arpa"] = r["mrr"] / r["cust_end"]
        r["churn_rate"] = r["churned"] / r["cust_beg"]
        r["net_adds"] = r["new"] - r["churned"]
        r["contribution"] = r["mrr"] - r["cogs"] - r["sm"]
        r["contribution_margin"] = r["contribution"] / r["mrr"]
        r["arr_per_fte"] = r["arr"] / r["headcount"]
        r["cac_month"] = r["sm"] / r["new"]
        r["mom"] = (r["mrr"] / d[i - 1]["mrr"] - 1) if i else None
        r["yoy"] = (r["mrr"] / d[i - 12]["mrr"] - 1) if i >= 12 else None
        # trailing-twelve-month unit economics (needs 12 months of history)
        if i >= 11:
            w = d[i - 11:i + 1]
            t_sm = sum(x["sm"] for x in w)
            t_new = sum(x["new"] for x in w)
            t_mrr = sum(x["mrr"] for x in w)
            t_cogs = sum(x["cogs"] for x in w)
            r["cac_ttm"] = t_sm / t_new
            r["gm_ttm"] = (t_mrr - t_cogs) / t_mrr
            r["churn_ttm"] = sum(x["churned"] for x in w) / sum(x["cust_beg"] for x in w)
            r["lifetime_months"] = 1 / r["churn_ttm"]
            r["ltv"] = r["arpa"] * r["gm_ttm"] / r["churn_ttm"]
            r["payback_months"] = r["cac_ttm"] / (r["arpa"] * r["gm_ttm"])
            r["ltv_cac"] = r["ltv"] / r["cac_ttm"]
        else:
            for k in ("cac_ttm", "gm_ttm", "churn_ttm", "lifetime_months", "ltv",
                      "payback_months", "ltv_cac"):
                r[k] = None
    return d


def quarters(d):
    """Group into calendar quarters; magic number needs the prior quarter."""
    qs = []
    for k in range(0, len(d) - 2, 3):
        w = d[k:k + 3]
        y, m = w[0]["month"].split("-")
        qs.append(dict(
            label=f"{y[2:]}Q{(int(m) - 1) // 3 + 1}",
            months=w,
            exit_mrr=w[-1]["mrr"],
            exit_arr=w[-1]["arr"],
            sm=sum(x["sm"] for x in w),
            new=sum(x["new"] for x in w),
            churned=sum(x["churned"] for x in w),
            mrr=sum(x["mrr"] for x in w),
            cogs=sum(x["cogs"] for x in w),
            cust_end=w[-1]["cust_end"],
        ))
    for i, q in enumerate(qs):
        prev = qs[i - 1] if i else None
        q["net_new_arr"] = q["exit_arr"] - prev["exit_arr"] if prev else None
        q["magic"] = (q["net_new_arr"] / prev["sm"]) if prev else None
        q["gm"] = (q["mrr"] - q["cogs"]) / q["mrr"]
        q["qoq"] = (q["exit_mrr"] / prev["exit_mrr"] - 1) if prev else None
    return qs


def arr_bridge(d, months=12):
    """Approximate 12-month ARR bridge.

    New and churned ARR are valued at each month's blended ARPA; whatever is
    left over is expansion/price. See the assumptions slide - this is an
    estimate, not cohort-level truth.
    """
    w = d[-months:]
    opening = d[-months - 1]["arr"]
    new = sum(x["new"] * x["arpa"] * 12 for x in w)
    churn = -sum(x["churned"] * x["arpa"] * 12 for x in w)
    closing = w[-1]["arr"]
    expansion = closing - opening - new - churn
    return dict(opening=opening, new=new, expansion=expansion, churn=churn,
                closing=closing)


# ---- last board deck, slide 7 (Q2 board update, "end of Q2") ----
SLIDE7 = {
    "CAC (trailing 12 months)": 1583.00,
    "LTV": 8019.93,
    "CAC payback (months)": 6.44,
    "ARPA": 236.27,
}


def reconcile(d):
    """Compare slide 7 of last quarter's board deck to current computed values."""
    r = d[-1]
    alt_cac = sum(x["sm"] for x in d) / (r["cust_end"] - STARTING_CUSTOMERS)
    return [
        dict(metric="ARPA", slide=SLIDE7["ARPA"], now=r["arpa"], fmt="money",
             verdict="Ties out",
             note="MRR / period-end active customers. Matches to the cent."),
        dict(metric="CAC payback (months)", slide=SLIDE7["CAC payback (months)"],
             now=r["payback_months"], fmt="num", verdict="Ties out",
             note="CAC / (ARPA x TTM gross margin). Reproduces at CAC = "
                  f"${r['cac_ttm']:,.0f} - not at the $1,583 on the same slide."),
        dict(metric="CAC (trailing 12 months)", slide=SLIDE7["CAC (trailing 12 months)"],
             now=r["cac_ttm"], fmt="money", verdict="CONFLICT",
             note="Slide overstates CAC by 35%. No trailing-12-month window of "
                  "S&M / new customers produces $1,583; dividing all-period S&M by "
                  f"NET adds does (${alt_cac:,.0f}), i.e. churned logos were netted "
                  "out of the denominator."),
        dict(metric="LTV", slide=SLIDE7["LTV"], now=r["ltv"], fmt="money",
             verdict="Definition gap",
             note="Slide is within rounding of ARPA x TTM GM / average monthly "
                  "churn rate ($8,029). We use TTM churn on a customer-weighted "
                  "basis, which is the more conservative denominator."),
    ]


def headline(d):
    r, qs = d[-1], quarters(d)
    return dict(
        month=r["month"], arr=r["arr"], mrr=r["mrr"], yoy=r["yoy"],
        customers=r["cust_end"], arpa=r["arpa"], gm=r["gm"],
        churn=r["churn_rate"], churn_ttm=r["churn_ttm"], cac=r["cac_ttm"],
        ltv=r["ltv"], ltv_cac=r["ltv_cac"], payback=r["payback_months"],
        headcount=r["headcount"], arr_per_fte=r["arr_per_fte"],
        magic=qs[-1]["magic"], contribution_margin=r["contribution_margin"],
        arr_growth_36m=r["arr"] / d[0]["arr"],
    )


def all_metrics():
    d = enrich(load())
    return d, quarters(d), headline(d), reconcile(d), arr_bridge(d)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    d, qs, h, rec, br = all_metrics()
    for k, v in h.items():
        print(f"{k:22s} {v}")
    print(br)
    for x in rec:
        print(x["metric"], x["slide"], round(x["now"], 2), x["verdict"])

"""Charts for the investor deck. Light surface, validated categorical palette."""
import os
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
import lib_metrics as L

OUT = "out/charts"
BLUE, ORANGE, AQUA, RED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#e34948"
INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#8a8880", "#e7e6e2"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "white", "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 11,
    "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "text.color": INK,
    "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "axes.titlesize": 12.5,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold", "axes.titlecolor": INK, "axes.titlepad": 12,
})

money = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"${v/1e6:.1f}M" if abs(v) >= 1e6 else f"${v/1e3:.0f}k")
pct = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v*100:.0f}%")
dollars = FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"${v:,.0f}")


def style(ax, ylab=None):
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color(GRID)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=1, zorder=0)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if ylab:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylab, fontsize=10)


def xmonths(ax, d, step=6):
    idx = list(range(len(d)))
    ax.set_xticks(idx[::step])
    ax.set_xticklabels([d[i]["month"] for i in idx[::step]], fontsize=9)


def endlabel(ax, x, y, text, color):
    ax.annotate(text, (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(-6, 12),
                ha="right", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color=color)


def fig(name, ncols=2, w=11.5, h=4.0):
    f, axes = plt.subplots(1, ncols, figsize=(w, h))
    return f, (axes if ncols > 1 else [axes]), name


def save(f, name):
    f.tight_layout(pad=1.6)
    f.savefig(f"{OUT}/{name}.png", dpi=200)
    plt.close(f)


def growth(d, qs):
    f, ax, n = fig("growth")
    y = [r["arr"] for r in d]
    ax[0].plot(range(len(d)), y, lw=2, color=BLUE, zorder=3)
    ax[0].fill_between(range(len(d)), y, color=BLUE, alpha=0.10, zorder=2)
    ax[0].set_title("ARR ($, exit month)")
    ax[0].yaxis.set_major_formatter(money)
    style(ax[0]); xmonths(ax[0], d)
    endlabel(ax[0], len(d) - 1, y[-1], f"${y[-1]/1e6:.2f}M", BLUE)

    q = [x for x in qs if x["net_new_arr"] is not None]
    ax[1].bar([x["label"] for x in q], [x["net_new_arr"] for x in q],
              color=BLUE, width=0.62, zorder=3)
    ax[1].set_title("Net new ARR added per quarter ($)")
    ax[1].yaxis.set_major_formatter(money)
    style(ax[1])
    ax[1].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=8.5)
    save(f, n)


def customers(d):
    f, ax, n = fig("customers")
    y = [r["cust_end"] for r in d]
    ax[0].plot(range(len(d)), y, lw=2, color=BLUE, zorder=3)
    ax[0].fill_between(range(len(d)), y, color=BLUE, alpha=0.10, zorder=2)
    ax[0].set_title("Active customers (period end)")
    style(ax[0]); xmonths(ax[0], d)
    endlabel(ax[0], len(d) - 1, y[-1], f"{y[-1]}", BLUE)

    c = [r["churn_rate"] for r in d]
    t = [r["churn_ttm"] for r in d]
    ax[1].plot(range(len(d)), c, lw=1.6, color=MUTED, zorder=3, label="Monthly logo churn")
    ax[1].plot(range(len(d)), t, lw=2.4, color=ORANGE, zorder=4, label="Trailing 12-month average")
    ax[1].set_title("Logo churn rate (% of opening customers)")
    ax[1].yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v*100:.1f}%"))
    ax[1].set_ylim(0, max(c) * 1.25)
    style(ax[1]); xmonths(ax[1], d)
    ax[1].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="lower left", labelcolor=INK2)
    save(f, n)


def margins(d):
    f, ax, n = fig("margins")
    y = [r["arpa"] for r in d]
    ax[0].plot(range(len(d)), y, lw=2, color=BLUE, zorder=3)
    ax[0].set_title("ARPA — MRR per active customer ($/mo)")
    ax[0].yaxis.set_major_formatter(dollars)
    style(ax[0]); xmonths(ax[0], d)
    endlabel(ax[0], len(d) - 1, y[-1], f"${y[-1]:.0f}", BLUE)

    g = [r["gm"] for r in d]
    ax[1].plot(range(len(d)), g, lw=2, color=AQUA, zorder=3)
    ax[1].set_title("Gross margin (MRR less COGS)")
    ax[1].yaxis.set_major_formatter(pct)
    ax[1].set_ylim(min(g) - 0.04, max(g) + 0.04)
    style(ax[1]); xmonths(ax[1], d)
    endlabel(ax[1], len(d) - 1, g[-1], f"{g[-1]*100:.1f}%", AQUA)
    save(f, n)


def unit_econ(d):
    w = [r for r in d if r["cac_ttm"]]
    f, ax, n = fig("unit_econ")
    y = [r["cac_ttm"] for r in w]
    ax[0].plot(range(len(w)), y, lw=2, color=ORANGE, zorder=3)
    ax[0].set_title("CAC, trailing 12 months (S&M / new customers)")
    ax[0].yaxis.set_major_formatter(dollars)
    ax[0].set_ylim(0, max(y) * 1.3)
    style(ax[0]); xmonths(ax[0], w, 4)
    endlabel(ax[0], len(w) - 1, y[-1], f"${y[-1]:,.0f}", ORANGE)
    ax[0].axhline(L.SLIDE7["CAC (trailing 12 months)"], color=RED, lw=1.6, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=4)
    ax[0].annotate("last board deck: $1,583", (0.5, L.SLIDE7["CAC (trailing 12 months)"]),
                   textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 6), fontsize=9, color=RED)

    p = [r["payback_months"] for r in w]
    ax[1].plot(range(len(w)), p, lw=2, color=BLUE, zorder=3)
    ax[1].set_title("CAC payback (months of gross profit)")
    ax[1].set_ylim(0, max(p) * 1.35)
    style(ax[1]); xmonths(ax[1], w, 4)
    ax[1].axhline(12, color=AQUA, lw=1.6, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=4)
    ax[1].annotate("12-month benchmark", (0.3, 12), textcoords="offset points",
                   xytext=(0, 6), fontsize=9, color=AQUA)
    endlabel(ax[1], len(w) - 1, p[-1], f"{p[-1]:.1f} mo", BLUE)
    save(f, n)


def efficiency(d, qs):
    f, ax, n = fig("efficiency")
    q = [x for x in qs if x["magic"] is not None]
    ax[0].bar([x["label"] for x in q], [x["magic"] for x in q], color=BLUE, width=0.62, zorder=3)
    ax[0].axhline(0.75, color=AQUA, lw=1.6, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=4)
    ax[0].annotate("0.75 = efficient-growth threshold", (0.0, 0.78), fontsize=9, color=AQUA)
    ax[0].set_title("SaaS magic number (net new ARR / prior-quarter S&M)")
    style(ax[0])
    ax[0].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, labelsize=8.5)

    y = [r["arr_per_fte"] for r in d]
    ax[1].plot(range(len(d)), y, lw=2, color=ORANGE, zorder=3)
    ax[1].set_title("ARR per FTE ($)")
    ax[1].yaxis.set_major_formatter(money)
    style(ax[1]); xmonths(ax[1], d)
    endlabel(ax[1], len(d) - 1, y[-1], f"${y[-1]/1e3:.0f}k", ORANGE)
    save(f, n)


def bridge(br):
    f, ax, n = fig("bridge", ncols=1, w=8.6, h=4.2)
    a = ax[0]
    labels = ["ARR\nSep-25", "New\ncustomers", "Expansion /\nprice", "Churned\ncustomers", "ARR\nSep-26"]
    vals = [br["opening"], br["new"], br["expansion"], br["churn"], br["closing"]]
    colors = [MUTED, AQUA, BLUE, RED, MUTED]
    base, bottoms = br["opening"], []
    for i, v in enumerate(vals):
        if i in (0, 4):
            bottoms.append(0)
        else:
            bottoms.append(base if v >= 0 else base + v)
            base += v
    heights = [vals[0], abs(vals[1]), abs(vals[2]), abs(vals[3]), vals[4]]
    a.bar(labels, heights, bottom=bottoms, color=colors, width=0.6, zorder=3)

HDR = Font(bold=True, size=10, color=NAVY)

THIN = Side(style="thin", color="D6DCE8")
BOX = Border(left=THIN, right=THIN, top=THIN, bottom=THIN)

MONEY = '#,##0.00;[Red](#,##0.00)'
MONEY0 = '#,##0;[Red](#,##0)'

def title(ws, text, sub=None, width=None):
    ws["A1"] = text
    ws["A1"].font = TITLE
    if sub:
        ws["A2"] = sub
        ws["A2"].font = SUB
    ws.sheet_view.showGridLines = False


def header_row(ws, row, labels, widths=None):
    for i, lab in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        c = ws.cell(row=row, column=i, value=lab)
        c.font = HDR
        c.fill = HDR_FILL
        c.border = BOX
        c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center", wrap_text=True)
    ws.row_dimensions[row].height = 30
    if widths:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths, start=1):
            ws.column_dimensions[ws.cell(row=row, column=i).column_letter].width = w


def fmt_col(ws, col, first, last, number_format, width=None):
    for r in range(first, last + 1):
        ws[f"{col}{r}"].number_format = number_format
    if width:
        ws.column_dimensions[col].width = width


def band(ws, first, last, ncols, every=2):
    for r in range(first, last + 1):
        if (r - first) % every == 1:
            for c in range(1, ncols + 1):
                ws.cell(row=r, column=c).fill = BAND_FILL


def note(ws, row, text, col="A"):
    ws[f"{col}{row}"] = text
    ws[f"{col}{row}"].font = SUB
    ws[f"{col}{row}"].alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="top")

Both files are under `./out/` (plus `out/charts/` with the source PNGs).

## The conflict with slide 7 — one number is wrong

| Metric | Board deck | Computed now | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CAC (TTM)** | **$1,583** | **$1,173** | **Conflict — overstated 35%** |
| LTV | $8,019.93 | $8,081.31 | Convention, 0.8% apart |
| CAC payback | 6.44 | 6.44 | Ties out |
| ARPA | $236.27 | $236.27 | Ties to the cent |

I reverse-engineered where $1,583 came from. On S&M ÷ **new** customers, no 12-month window in the 36 months produces it — every window lands between $950 and $1,173. It is reproduced almost exactly ($1,584) by S&M ÷ **net adds** over Feb-24 to Dec-25: churned logos were subtracted from the denominator, on a window already 9 months stale.

The slide also contradicts itself: its own 6.44-month payback only reconciles at a CAC of ~$1,173. So LTV:CAC was reported at ~5.1x when it was ~6.9x — understating the business.

## Headline numbers (Sep-2026)

ARR $2.15M (+70% YoY, 7.8x over 36 months) · 757 customers from 120 · ARPA $236 · gross margin 78% · logo churn 2.26%/mo TTM · CAC $1,173 · LTV $8,081 · LTV:CAC 6.9x · payback 6.4 months · magic number 1.72.

**One thing to know before this goes out:** the extract behaves like normalised management data, not a raw ledger — gross margin rises by *exactly* 17.1 bps in every one of the 36 months (72.00%→78.00%), and churned-logo counts step up on a fixed cadence. Reconcile it to the accounting system first. It's flagged on slide 11 and in the workbook README.

## What's in each file

**investor_update.pptx** (11 slides): title, headline KPIs, ARR growth, customers/retention, pricing & margin, unit economics, GTM efficiency, ARR bridge, the board-deck correction, quarterly scorecard, definitions & gaps.

**bluebell_saas_model.xlsx** (8 tabs): README, Assumptions, Input_Data, Monthly_Metrics (28 columns × 36 months), Quarterly, Unit_Economics (incl. CAC sensitivity across four conventions), Board_Recon, Projection. Only Input_Data and the blue Assumptions cells are hardcoded — everything else is a live formula, so your CFO can flex drivers and trace any number. I independently recalculated the workbook and confirmed every formula matches the Python engine.

## Assumptions I made

- **120 opening customers** seeds the roll-forward; every customer metric moves with it.
- **CAC** = TTM S&M ÷ TTM *new* logos (no netting) — the definition I'd recommend standardising on.
- **LTV** = ARPA × TTM gross margin ÷ TTM logo churn. The slide-7 figure used a simple average of monthly churn rates instead; both are defensible, hence 0.8%.
- **"Last quarter's board deck"** — ARPA ties exactly to Sep-2026, so I treated slide 7 as being on the same period rather than calendar Q2.
- **Sep-2026 treated as a complete month**, as supplied.
- **No burn or runway anywhere.** The extract has no R&D, G&A or payroll, so opex, EBITDA and Rule of 40 aren't computable. "Contribution" (MRR − COGS − S&M) is an upper bound on profitability, not burn. NRR is likewise not derivable — the ARR bridge treats expansion as a residual and says so on the chart.
